What makes Tennessee whiskey different from bourbon?

How should I store an opened bottle?
Keep it upright, out of direct sunlight, at room temperature. An opened bottle holds its character well for a year or more if the cap stays tight.
Is Jack Daniel's gluten-free?
Distillation removes gluten proteins, so the finished spirit contains none by the time it's bottled — though as a grain-derived product it isn't formally labelled gluten-free in every market.

Questions

What makes the production method special?
Instead of blending white champagne with a little still red wine, the common shortcut, Laurent-Perrier macerates whole Pinot Noir grapes with their skins for 48–72 hours before pressing — a slower, more demanding process that draws out real colour and genuine red-fruit aroma rather than just tinting the wine.
Why is 1968 significant?
That's when Bernard de Nonancourt introduced Cuvée Rosé, treating rosé as its own serious wine rather than a lesser variation of the house's white champagne — a decision that's made it the reference point most other rosé champagnes are still compared to.
What's the story behind the bottle shape?
It's inspired by a flask design associated with King Henri IV, giving Cuvée Rosé one of the most recognisable silhouettes in Champagne.
